content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Nineveh is most commonly treated as an emblem of a wicked, pagan society that stands under divine judgment but may receive divine mercy through repentance.","primary_basis":["Jonah 1:1-2 — Nineveh's wickedness comes before God.","Jonah 3:4-10 — Nineveh is warned of judgment, repents, and is spared.","Jonah 4:10-11 — God's compassion extends to the people of the pagan city.","Matthew 12:41 and Luke 11:29-32 — Jesus uses the repentant Ninevites to condemn a generation that refuses to repent.","Nahum 1:1-3; 2:13; 3:1-7 — Nineveh represents violent, arrogant imperial power brought under divine judgment."],"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Nineveh symbolizes oppressive worldly empire or political power destined for divine overthrow.","basis":["Nahum 2:1-13","Nahum 3:1-19","Zephaniah 2:13-15"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Nineveh represents the Gentile world as the object of God's missionary concern and compassion.","basis":["Jonah 3:1-10","Jonah 4:10-11"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The repentant people of Nineveh symbolize responsive Gentiles who contrast with unrepentant Israel or with those who reject Jesus.","basis":["Matthew 12:38-41","Luke 11:29-32"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Nineveh functions broadly as a type of the sinful world, comparable in some preaching to Babylon or other cities opposed to God.","basis":["Jonah 1:2","Nahum 3:1-7"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Nineveh symbolizes an individual's inner sinful nature, the flesh, or a specific ecclesiastical institution.","basis":["Such readings are generally allegorical and lack a standard biblical identification."],"prominence":"rare"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is no single settled symbolic definition of Nineveh across Christian interpretation. Its canonical portrayals differ: Jonah emphasizes pagan wickedness, repentance, mission, and mercy, while Nahum emphasizes imperial violence and irreversible judgment. The broadest recognizable synthesis is therefore a sinful pagan society accountable to God, capable of repentance, and otherwise subject to judgment."}
